speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: It ensures that public entertainment is carried out in a lawful and orderly manner, in line with standards of public decency, and at suitable places.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Consumer preferences change and business models evolve rapidly.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We have to constantly finetune the public entertainment regulatory regime to stay current and effective.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Currently, about four in five PE establishments have good track records of complying with licence conditions.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: A small group of errant establishments breach these conditions, do not cooperate with the Police and create law and order problems.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: MHA last amended PEMA in 2000 to improve the administration of public entertainment licences.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: MCI amended PEMA in 2014 to establish a framework for greater clarity and consistency in the regulation of arts entertainment.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: It is timely to update PEMA and ensure its relevancy.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: For the vast majority of licensees who are law-abiding, we will take a lighter touch to support the continued vibrancy of the industry.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: For instance, MHA will introduce licences with longer validity periods than the standard one-year licences that are issued to all PE establishments today.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The Police will also work closely with the industry to promote more responsible business operations.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: On the other hand, we need to strengthen regulatory levers against errant PE establishments.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The Bill proposes to make the necessary legislative amendments to support this enhanced regulatory regime.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: As part of the review, MHA consulted the PE industry through the Singapore Nightlife Business Association (SNBA).

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We reached out to close to 180 nightlife establishments.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: SNBA and these establishments support the proposed amendments in the Bill.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: MCI has also reviewed the arts entertainment-related provisions for greater consistency between the regulation of arts entertainment held at public entertainment establishments or events, which are licensable by the Police, and the regulation of arts entertainments held at other venues.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The amendments are intended to clarify that arts entertainment will be regulated in the same manner, regardless of whether it is held at PE establishments or events licensable by the Police, or at other venues.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The amendments do not entail any changes to existing arts entertainment content standards or the Info-Communications Media Development Authority's (IMDA's) arts entertainment classification and licensing processes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: MCI has engaged both the PE industry and the arts community on these amendments.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The first set of amendments seeks to prevent the operation of PE establishments that are either operated by unsuitable persons or businesses or operated in unsuitable locations.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Under the current section 5 of the Act, the Licensing Officer may require an applicant for a PE licence to satisfy certain criteria and requirements.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This existing provision allows the Licensing Officer to assess whether the applicant is fit and proper to carry on a PE business and prevent unsuitable persons from doing so.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Clause 6 of the Bill expands this assessment of applicant suitability to include persons who are related to the applicant, namely, the responsible officers and individuals with substantial interest in, or control or direction over the business of the applicant.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Clause 4 of the Bill defines "responsible officer" and it will cover directors of body corporates, partners of partnerships, and officers of unincorporated associations, as the case may be.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This ensures that all persons who can influence the decisions of the business are duly assessed and are not working behind the scenes to operate the PE establishment.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The Police have reviewed the criteria and requirements to be applied to both applicants and their related persons, and the updated criteria and requirements will be published on the Police's website in due course.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: One key objective of PEMA is to ensure that PE is carried out at suitable places.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Clause 4 creates a new provision that requires the Licensing Officer to take into account the Urban Redevelopment Authority's (URA's) planning considerations in approving a place to operate a PE establishment.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: For example, a Licensing Officer cannot approve applications for pubs and bars in a conservation area, to maintain the character of historic districts.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The Bill also proposes to increase the penalties for errant operators who try to circumvent our controls and safeguards altogether, by operating PE establishments without valid licences.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This amendment differentiates offences by licensees who contravene licence conditions or the Act, and such offences are currently subject to a maximum fine of $10,000.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The offender who disregarded the law entirely has to be treated more harshly than the offender who had obtained a licence but was not fully compliant with its conditions or the Act.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The maximum fine for providing PE without a valid licence will be raised to $20,000.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: In cases where licensees do not comply with licensing conditions or become unsuitable to operate a PE establishment, the Police must have the powers to deal effectively with them.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The second set of amendments will strengthen these powers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The Demerit Point System, introduced in 2000, allows the Police to adopt a graduated enforcement approach against licensees who infringe licence conditions.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Licensees are given demerit points for breaches, and appropriate action is taken depending on the number of demerit points accumulated over a two-year period.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The Police impose demerit points for licensing breaches that are compounded, or for which the licensee is convicted in Court.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: If the licensee is charged for multiple licensing breaches, it is usual for the Court to take into consideration a proportion of the charges for the purpose of sentencing, rather than convict the licensee for all charges.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Charges that are taken into consideration for purposes of sentencing currently do not attract demerit points.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The Demerit Point System provides early warning for minor breaches and encourages the licensee to exercise self-discipline.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: However, the Licensing Officer may immediately suspend or cancel the licence where the need arises.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Even so, section 14, subsection 1 only applies where the PE provided is problematic.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: These serious crimes must have a nexus with the establishment, but not necessarily the PE provided in the establishment.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This includes offences, such as drug offences, trafficking-in-persons and offences under the Organised Crime Act.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The list of serious crimes is specified in the new Second Schedule to the Bill.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This will allow the Police to immediately suspend PE establishments which are being used for such serious crimes, instead of waiting for Court trials on the cases to conclude.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This also deters other operators from using their establishments for unlawful activities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The third set of amendments enhances Police operational effectiveness in enforcing the Act.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Clause 5 of the Bill allows the Licensing Officer to appoint suitably trained individuals as "authorised persons".

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Clause 17 empowers authorised persons to conduct inspections at PE establishments and events.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Authorised persons will not be given the more specialised powers that Licensing Officer and Police officers have, for example, powers of forced entry and arrest.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: These provisions give the Police operational flexibility to deploy manpower more effectively or conduct more frequent checks if the need arises.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Clause 18 empowers Licensing Officers and Police Officers to enter premises, including using necessary force, if there is reasonable suspicion that offences under the Bill are being or has been committed within.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Today, appeals against the decision of the Licensing Officer are heard by the relevant Minister.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The PE Appeal Board will operate like the Liquor Appeal Board under the Liquor Control Act.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The Minister for Home Affairs will appoint the members of the Board.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The intent is to appoint members from diverse fields, including legal, education and business.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The Appeal Board will receive representations from the Licensing Officer and the appellant, and make a decision based on simple majority.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Its decision on the merits of the case will be final.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: On behalf of the Minister responsible for arts entertainment, I will now address MCI's proposed amendments in the Bill.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The first two sets of amendments by MCI deal with the classification of arts entertainment, while the third relates to appeals against IMDA's classification decisions.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: For arts entertainment licensed by IMDA under the Bill, IMDA may impose conditions as part of the arts entertainment licence.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: However, for arts entertainment held at PE establishments or events, IMDA will not be able to impose such conditions within the PE licence issued by the Police.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Clause 12 allows IMDA to impose the conditions as part of IMDA's classification of the arts entertainment held at PE establishments or events, thereby giving these conditions the same effect as licensing conditions imposed by IMDA.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The second set of amendments involves arts entertainment content that exceeds the maximum R18 rating under the Arts Entertainment Classification Code (AECC).

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Currently, IMDA will not issue arts entertainment licences for such arts entertainment content.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: However, this does not apply for PE establishments or events.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Clause 13 clarifies that IMDA may refuse to classify such arts entertainment content regardless of whether it is held at PE establishments or events or at other venues.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The third set of amendments relates to appeals against IMDA's classification decisions.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Appealable decisions refer to IMDA's classification ratings, its refusal to classify content that exceeds the maximum R18 rating under AECC and the imposition of conditions as part of its classification of arts entertainment.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: I will now touch briefly on other amendments of the Bill.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Clause 16 clarifies that the Ministers charged with the responsibility for PEs and arts entertainments respectively have the powers to make exemptions for their respective areas.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The regulation of meetings, such as rallies, talks and forums, now falls under the Public Order Act, which was enacted in 2009.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I approve of the more stringent assessments during licence applications to screen out undesirable operators and the harsher penalties proposed.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: These measures will greatly help to act as deterrents.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I am worried about the increasingly liberal attitude of our young people towards drugs, as found in a survey released last month by the National Council Against Drug Abuse (NCADA).

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In fact, today's Straits Times' article on the increasing number of new psychoactive substances causing harm to their users is most worrying.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Entertainment outlets, such as nightclubs, are popular venues for young people to congregate, make friends and have fun.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: There, they are especially open to new and exciting experiences and, hence, very vulnerable to taking higher risks as they experiment with perceived "adult consumables", such as smoking, alcohol or drugs.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Even those who are less inclined may give in due to peer pressure.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We must ensure a safe environment for them to have clean fun and protect them from the ravages of drugs.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Numerous raids by our Home Team over the years had also unearthed vice activities upon the premises of unscrupulous operators.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In addition to the crimes of human trafficking, such activities are also a threat to our health system, as sex workers may spread sexually transmitted infections.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Singapore's night scene has become quite vibrant and attracts foreigners and those who traffic in them out for a quick buck.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This is clearly undesirable due to numerous externalities, such as petty crimes, organised crimes, homicides and so forth.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: PE venues also include Internet cafes, which can be located within or near housing estates.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Again, many of the patrons of such outlets are from the younger age groups.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This is one of the few ways to expedite the progress of investigations.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We should provide our Police Officers more support and leeway to perform their duties and nip criminal activities in the bud.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: While I support the Bill's overall aims, I have two sets of queries on the Bill regarding PE licensing and enforcement.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The licensing of PE establishments vests in the Licensing Officer.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: For those who wish to appeal against the Licensing Officer's decisions, the Bill proposes the setting up of a new PE Appeal Board to replace the Minister as the appellate authority in certain types of appeals.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: At the same time, other appeals will continue to go to the Minister.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Is it the intention to let the Appeal Board hear appeals which may be of a more routine nature, while the Minister retains the power to hear appeals in more difficult or complex cases?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Or is it vice versa, with the Appeal Board dealing with the more difficult appeals?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: My second set of queries relates to enforcement as set out in clauses 17 and 18 of the Bill.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Clause 17 amends the current Act significantly in terms of the right of entry and inspection of enforcement officers.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The current Act empowers the Licensing Officer and Police Officers to enter premises to ascertain if licensing conditions are complied with.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The Bill will include a new category of officer, called an "authorised person", who, together with the Licensing Officer and Police Officers, will be called "inspecting officers".

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: These inspecting officers will be given enhanced enforcement powers to enter and inspect PE outlets.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: But it is also true that the Bill gives these authorised persons enhanced powers in confrontational scenarios, such as requiring production of information, accessing computers, interviewing suspects on site, and requiring witnesses to provide explanations of documents or information found.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The category of the new "authorised persons" to be included to exercise these enhanced powers deserves some attention.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: According to clause 5 of the Bill, an individual may be appointed as an "authorised person" if he is "suitably trained".

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: If the Government is referring to Auxiliary Police Officers (APOs) becoming authorised officers for licensing inspections, does their training cover the necessary skill competencies to handle the confrontational scenarios envisaged in clause 17?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I would like a clarification on why it is deemed necessary now to provide the Licensing Officer expressly with powers of forced entry when he seems to have managed his duties all these decades without such an explicit power.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My concern is largely with those establishments which may create disamenities or inconveniences within their immediate community.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: There are establishments within my constituency, located close to residences, which provide PE, such as karaoke singing or telecast of sports matches.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While most of these establishments adhere to existing laws on PE, I have received feedback from residents about a couple of these establishments.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: One feedback is on noise, especially into the late night.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Another feedback is illegal parking along the roads and driveways to houses, especially those in the private landed estates.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Another feedback is on activities that may create feelings of discomfort among residents living nearby, or feedback on establishments that are suspected of allowing illicit activities to take place within and around their premises.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have a few clarifications with regard to the proposed amendments.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Clause 5, amendment to section 4, mentioned that the appropriate licensing officer may appoint an individual, who need not be a public officer, but who is suitably trained as an authorised person to carry out certain functions of the Act.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: First, what is the extent of functions of the Bill that this appointed individual will be able to execute?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Second, what are the criteria in appointing the individual to carry out these functions?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Is there a maximum number of demerit points that a licensee can accumulate before having the licence suspended or revoked?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Would this be similar to our driving licence demerit points system?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Notwithstanding these clarifications, Mdm Speaker, I support the amendments in the Bill.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: These are important amendments in support of our fight against racketeering and associated criminal activities.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I wish to seek clarification on the following five areas of this Bill.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: My Parliamentary colleagues, Dr Intan and Ms Sylvia Lim, also spoke about this point.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: It appears that under the proposed amendments, these persons would be deemed as public servants when exercising their powers under the Act.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This is in contrast to the Liquor Control (Supply and Consumption) Act 2015, which only provides for APOs or Police Officers to be an approved person under that Act to carry out licensing functions.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: How will these private sector vendors be selected and are there other similar uses of the private sector for licensing or other analogous matters in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Second, the proposed amendments to section 5 of the Act expands the criteria for obtaining a licence which presently only stipulates operational requirements, to include criteria and requirements relating to the responsible officer of the applicant of the licence.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The explanatory notes of the Bill state that this takes into account considerations of whether the responsible officer is a fit and proper person, similar to the approach taken in the Liquor Control (Supply and Consumption) Act.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Could the Parliamentary Secretary please clarify whether proceedings include investigations that have been commenced against the licensee even if the licensee has not been formally charged in Court with any offence yet?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Would proceedings also include proceedings for a confiscation order, for example, under the Organised Crime Act, even if the licensee or the responsible officer has not been the subject of any criminal proceedings in respect of an offence stipulated in the proposed Second Schedule of the Bill?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Additionally, how would the proposed amendment to section 14 take into account foreign proceedings commenced against the licensee or the responsible officer, say, for example, a vice-related offence which has an equivalent in the proposed Second Schedule?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The proposed section 14(2A) presently does not take into account such foreign proceedings.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Yet, this may be relevant, especially if the licensee or the responsible officer is involved in operating similar businesses in other countries and foreign proceedings have been brought against him in that regard.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Alternatively, would such considerations be instead taken into account in the fit and proper criteria to determine whether the licence should be suspended or cancelled under the proposed amendments to section 14(2) of the Act?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: If so, would there be a need to widen the language used in that provision to include responsible officers of the licensees and persons having substantial control over these licensees?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Could the hon Parliamentary Secretary please clarify what sorts of conditions are contemplated?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Would the Ministry also be providing guidelines on how the discretion to impose conditions would be exercised?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This would promote greater certainty for producers of the arts, who could then have these guidelines in mind at the outset when planning and producing their art exhibitions and performances.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I note now that two relevant appeal authorities have been proposed in respect of appeals against appealable decisions of the PE Licensing Officer, namely, the newly constituted PE Appeal Board for decisions involving prescribed specified establishments or a prescribed class of licensees and, in any other cases, to the Minister responsible for PE.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Could the Parliamentary Secretary please elaborate on what type of specified establishments or class of licensees would be prescribed that would involve the PE Appeal Board?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I believe a similar point was raised by the hon Member Ms Sylvia Lim.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In addition, what is the rationale for having an independent PE Appeal Board that deals with appeals against certain decisions involving these prescribed specified establishments or class of licensees, whilst appeals against all other decisions continue to be dealt with by the Minister?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I support our efforts to promote higher standards amongst PE operators, and to safeguard against those who misuse these premises to carry out racketeering activities.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I also applaud both Ministries' efforts in engaging the stakeholders before tabling this Bill.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: They contribute to the vibrancy of our cityscape.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: They also form an important part of our tourism industry.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: If they serve as the front for illegal activities, they will undermine the appeal of legitimate businesses.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: If they thrive by allowing activities on their premises that properly run establishments adhering to strict regulations refuse to accommodate, the latter could be edged out of business competition.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: In particular, I would like to express my concerns about unruly behaviour regularly linked to PE outlets.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: The setting is usually the same, with the victim confronted by a group of attackers in the hours between midnight and dawn.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: Unfortunately, this was hardly the first time an incident of this type occurred.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: On Christmas eve of 2015, an American who worked as a stuntman was killed in a brawl at a different area reportedly after he was caught up in an attack by a large group.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: In fact, merely going by insider accounts reported in media exposes alone would tell us that when a serious incident occurs, it is just a spillover from what happens within these establishments on a regular basis.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: A report published in The Straits Times on 19 March this year which followed up on the March incident, gave accounts from three perspectives − those of the regular patrons, employees and establishment owners.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: They all concurred that such incidents were not one-off.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: Of course, some laid the blame on bad press, too, which could mean quite a lot of different things, depending on how you look at it.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: When incidents are reported, such as fights and even deaths, the same places/names regularly turn up.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: What is worse is to hear young people talk about what happens regularly that goes on unreported as though it was the most natural thing in the world on a night out.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: The current Bill deals with what occurs on the premises of such establishments, but we often hear of reported incidents occurring outside.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: This happens so regularly that when it is reported, I often wonder why there is no attempt to draw a link to the establishments where such incidents could have originated.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: When violence peaks and serious incidents occur, it is the Police which have to be called in.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: At such times, the diversion of significant Police resources is more than just a cost that has to be borne by taxpayers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: The drain on tight Police resources caused by recurrent incidents of this nature is a distraction from greater policing priorities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: When nightspots tolerate or engage in undesirable activities on their premises, young patrons are especially vulnerable.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: Not only could they be unwitting victims of such incidents, if they are led to think that illegal activities can proceed without effective policing, they may come to associate them as a natural part of an exciting night out.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: The violence and deaths which have occurred are both senseless and tragic.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I am the local Member of Parliament (MP) in the Kampong Glam and Jalan Besar vicinity.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Most important to many residents − not just in my area, but I think in other areas as well − the Bill will strengthen the ability of the Government to ensure that PE is not carried out in places that are not suitable to its nature.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: As MPs serving residents in the city district, colleagues such as Mr Melvin Yong, previously Mr Edwin Tong and myself, have had our fair share of challenges to balance the tension between the needs of residents and the needs of PE outlets and events.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Along Queen Street several years ago, the problems of noise, especially from customers arriving and leaving, drinking during hours when nearby residents are sleeping, had resulted in many complaints to the Police and also gave rise to Police raids.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Then, at Little India, where merchants organise live concerts to attract visitors, including tourists and foreign workers, residents, young and old, in nearby public housing, could not accept the resulting noise and crowds and often called up Member Melvin and myself.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Third, at mixed developments, such as Sultan Plaza and the Textile Centre, the nearby night joints created at one time much unhappiness to the local residents living upstairs.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This had resulted in many night phone calls to the Police, to the MP and Police raids as well, creating much tension between the residents and the nightspot operators.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And then, where religious activities take place in establishments, such as mosques in my Kampong Glam area, there had also been constant tension with the neighbouring food and beverage (F&B) and entertainment outlets whose offerings may be considered potentially offensive to some who go to the mosque to worship.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: But kudos to the diligent Singapore Police Force, the Home Team members who are based at, especially Marina Bay and the Rochor Police Posts, incidents are markedly reduced over the years.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This peace is, however, achieved not without the high cost of enforcement by the Police and the supporting efforts of the local grassroots helpers and the MPs.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This is due to the disamenities that will most certainly arise.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Disamenity issues, such as the issues of noise, that would still occur when customers arrive and leave through even sound-proofed doors, and often during the resting hours of residents.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Although the Home Team brigades I work with are some of the most diligent and helpful public servants I know, on behalf of my residents, I still urge the Government to consider the following measures.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: One, adopt a whole-of-Government approach, with relevant agencies, besides MHA, URA, the Ministry of National Development (MND), the Housing and Development Board (HDB) and the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) as well, to ensure a more appropriate tenant mix of businesses with the right licences in residential estates.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: There should be more community services located closer to the residents, such as senior activity centres, preschools, childcare centres, polyclinics, grocery stores that will be useful to the residents.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This should be part of urban planning zoning for residential estates in the city.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: A more family-friendly wholesome tenant mix in residential areas will certainly save considerable amounts of resources to monitor, track, raid and arrest potential culprits.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: It sounds sexy and good but it is really hard to implement, especially if these mixed developments for residential and commercial are within the same building.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Nightclubs, massage parlours, bars and entertainment outlets in buildings with residents living above is a sure recipe for conflicts and tension as they are most likely always the sources of complaints and conflicts.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: First, on the amendment of section 4 that provides for the Licensing Officer to appoint "individuals who are suitably trained" to perform the powers of inspection and other duties of the Licensing Officer.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: About these authorised persons, I would like to ask the Ministry on the extent of power that may be exercised by them and also the courses of action should a normal routine procedure escalate to a full-blown public disorder or even a riot situation.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Second, on the amendment of section 15A, whilst I understand the need to align the two areas of licences by MHA and MCI, I would like to seek clarification so that things will be more transparent on the decision framework that the Arts Entertainment Licensing Officer may impose in classifying any arts entertainment.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Lastly, I would like to seek clarification on the PE Appeal Board, which is one of the additions to the Bill, as to the reasons for setting this up and the scope of this Board, the Board's decision-making framework and approach and how this might be different from the current arrangements.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I look forward to the Parliamentary Secretary's considered response.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: The world order is changing at breakneck speed and people's preferences and desires are similarly being transformed.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: As our society matures with changing times, technological advances are taking precedence in all sectors, including the arts and entertainment.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: As Singapore safeguards itself against the constant threats of various forms, a tighter control over PE events seems to be a necessary evil.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: As this may impact the creativity element of individuals, groups, businesses and organisations which put together such events, the Government needs to maintain a fair balance.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: When control measures with tighter licensing requirements are introduced to protect the safety and security of the society, it is important to ensure that creative efforts are not stifled.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: However, Madam, I have the following clarifications in regard to the Bill.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: There needs to be greater clarity on the separation of public meetings from PE.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Both PE and public meetings need to be in line with community standards and public decency and uphold the law and public order.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Two, there needs to be more clarity on the purpose of this Bill.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: What are some of the examples that were refused and suspended before?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: And what were the bases for refusing and suspending these licences?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: It is important to have an independent body so that the system gains trust from the public by ensuring openness and transparency.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Who will appoint and who will be appointed as members of the Appeal Board?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: If the appeal is rejected, will there be recourse for the aggrieved party?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Has there been an increase of such cases of conducting PE without a licence?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Being a strong proponent of public education and awareness, I would like to propose that we channel the funds collected from these fines into public education.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Will there be a periodic review of the classifications of the various PE and arts as well as licensing requirements?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, the number and variety of PE and arts entertainment activities are likely to rise in the months ahead.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This is a good sign as this suggests that more Singaporeans are becoming more appreciative and receptive towards various cultures, artforms, sports events and so forth.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Moreover, the abundance of entertainment, many from overseas, reflect our nation's openness and acceptance of different cultures.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: All said, we should also respect the values of our own Asian culture and not allow individuals or groups to misuse art to become an affront to others.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Worse, if they are used to promote radical ideology.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I am pleased to note that stricter guidelines and policing policies have been introduced to be stricter on operators of places of entertainment.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I believe the management should do more than just deploying bouncers.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But they should have ground staff who would see to it that the safety of the patrons is safeguarded.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Those who allow drugs to be sold on their premises should be charged.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: They should never allow the use of illicit means to draw the crowd.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: While it is easy for licence owners to point a finger at its employees, I feel the owners should not run the business by proxy.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Would this screening apply to their key staff running the operations?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: To date, how many owners have been taken to task or charged for violating the licensing conditions?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Will those holding licences now and found unsuitable under this new Bill be asked to surrender their licence?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Are foreigners allowed to apply for a licence?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: If so, how are they to be held responsible?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Government Ministries must coordinate their efforts or we would end up wasting public funds.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This is like, on the one hand, so many jackpot machines were allowed at a soccer club when, on the other, we watched over licensed casinos like a hawk and impose entry fees for locals.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The downside of drinking is that when one gets one too many, rowdy behaviour, sometimes culminating in brawls, would occur.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: One incident that came to mind was the tragic case of an American stuntman, who was badly beaten up outside a club and succumbed to his injuries.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Recently, we read of a fatal stabbing hours after the night club shuttered its doors to the last customer.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Our Police, Customs, Immigration officers are stretched in this era of constant threat of terrorism, where they have to protect our shoreline.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I take pride in the efficiency of our MHA.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We should impose greater responsibility on the operators of these night spots to provide the protection to the public and maintain good order.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Can it be made mandatory for nightlife spots to hire better qualified and trained security officers to maintain public order inside and outside the premises?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Next, what is the guideline for the approval of locations for nightlife spots?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: There are a few pubs and games arcades along Sembawang Road, which is near Goodlink Park, and I have been receiving feedback from residents.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: They complain about cigarette butts, littering, noise, public nuisance and so on.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Some residents are worried about the bad influence on their children.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I have given the feedback to URA, and URA replied that this is not under their purview because the games arcades are registered under the Registry of Societies, which is under MHA.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, MHA told me that they will monitor, but until now, residents are still living under all these influences and pressures that they do not like to have.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Some of these nightlife spots are sleazy, with scantily-clad women openly soliciting business, and drunk and rowdy customers creating a public nuisance.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: It can be disturbing and dangerous for residents walking through the area.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: On a related note, are there guidelines for the attire of employees working in these establishments?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I note that there are strict guidelines pertaining to attire at public events, particularly those of performers and even staff.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Should these guidelines not also be extended to the employees who loiter outside their establishments?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: (In Mandarin):   The main purpose of these amendments is to regulate public entertainment.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: However, I would like to talk about our PE places.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: These places can bring about two types of problems.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Do we require security personnel at these places to undergo extra training to stop the fighting?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This will reduce the burden on our Police Force, as well as potential harm caused by these fights.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Residents living nearby will also experience less inconveniences.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The second problem is the noise and the scantily-clad women loitering outside these places.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: They cause discomfort to the residents living nearby.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Can the authorities clarify there is a minimum distance requirement between these places and residential areas?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Should there be guidelines for the attire of employees who loiter outside their establishments, just like the guidelines pertaining to attire of PE performers?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: (In English): Mdm Speaker, I support the Bill and I believe that the need to protect the patrons are important, be it against drug abuse, fire or unnecessary fights between patrons.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: PEMA provides for the regulation of PE and meetings and helps ensure that these are carried out within acceptable community standards and public decency as well as uphold our law and order.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: This is also linked to the act of allowing the officers mentioned to enter premises suspected of flouting regulations under this Bill, even if they have been denied entry by the owners.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Blacklisting these errant personalities and companies is critical, as, in many cases, they tend to commit recurrent breaches.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: But these people end up circulating in the industry, giving a negative perception and name to the industry.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: It is thus unfair to the others who are genuinely interested in providing such services honestly.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: These days, the trend is to have the so-called artistic entertainment on showcase at non-traditional venues and locations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Information technology (IT) also enables live streaming from remote locations, including overseas locations and sites.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Thus, can we ensure the stakeholders are clear on the classification and categorisation?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Can the Ministry also help with more education and publicity, so that people can have a better idea of the latest regulations in place?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: And of what severity or seriousness levels are these?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Can I also clarify with the Minister what exactly is meant by the term "a fit and proper person" in this Bill?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: I feel that it is better for us to clarify this definition upfront, rather than have to be contradicted by applicants in the process of their application later on after we have passed the Bill.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Pertaining to the PE Appeal Board, what exactly is the composition of the Board, and what is the SOP and terms of reference and so on and so forth?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: As has been asked by other Members as well, can I also request that perhaps the local MP for such premises can be consulted when there is such an appeal going on as well?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: For the demerit points system allocated under clause 11, can this be tagged to the person for a longer period because I feel that if you just dispose of this within one to two years, the seriousness that it should actually portray to these people may be lost?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Therefore, we want them to be more conscious of the seriousness of these things and the Bill.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This signals a need to tighten our laws regulating PE outlets.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: First, I agree with the proposal to tighten regulatory approval by requiring the Licensing Officer to consider whether the applicant is appropriate for the role.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This will send a strong signal to the licensees to keep their outlets in order.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, as highlighted by our Parliamentary colleagues, Er Dr Lee Bee Wah and Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef, one concern still lingers − the usage of proxies to apply for a PE licence.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How can we put an end to unsavoury businessmen operating from behind the scenes in the PE industry?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Next, I would like to highlight the need to tighten the approval of PE licences, especially in or near mixed developments.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Let us take the three examples in my constituency − Balmoral Plaza and Orchard Towers which are mixed developments, and the area around Mount Sophia, which is near Peace Centre.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Like Dr Intan Mokhtar and Ms Denise Phua, during my house visits, it is not uncommon to hear residents complain about these PE outlets located within or near their homes.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While fights take place regularly among drunken individuals, beyond such safety concerns, these outlets also bring about disamenities as their patrons loiter outside the outlet and indulge in loud conversations and smoking.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I believe enough has been elaborated by the various Members who have spoken before me.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Would the PE Appeal Board consider residents' appeals against the granting of a PE licence in their neighbourhood?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Feedback from residents can also be given to the Appeal Board either through the Management Corporation Strata Titles (MCSTs) or the Residents' Committees.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Residents tell me that in many of these PE outlets, the bouncers or security personnel will ask the patrons to smoke or fight outside of the outlets instead so that they will not get any demerit points or violate any licensing conditions.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Similar to what has been done at Orchard Towers, would the Police also consider setting up surveillance cameras outside selected PE outlets, in particular, where these outlets co-exist with residences?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This is to monitor the spillover activities from these outlets.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I especially support the amendment to section 14 of the Act, which allows the suspension of a licence when proceeding in relation to offences listed in the proposed Second Schedule.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We witnessed an active debate in Parliament recently on stamping out the use of drugs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The offences in the Second Schedule include drug offences, and I believe this is aligned with the move to make Singapore a drug-free society.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Further, the Second Schedule includes matters in relation to prostitution and human trafficking.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am supportive of this in light of the criticisms levelled against Singapore for not doing enough to combat human trafficking and protect foreign workers in this dark side of society.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is testament to the Government's continued commitment to prevent trafficking.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I note that a Licensing Officer may appoint a suitably trained individual as an authorised person.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As many Members of this House have asked, can the Parliamentary Secretary clarify what is meant by "suitably trained", who these authorised persons will be, and also clarify why there is a need to appoint these authorised persons in the first place?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I also understand that the Police will work with industry partners to promote higher standards.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Parliamentary Secretary clarify if these standards have already been drafted?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If not, when will they be ready, and also whether these standards will be published on the Police's website for transparency?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This will be in line with the "fit and proper" criteria details which will be published on the Police's website.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Parliamentary Secretary also clarify if the eventual goal is to legislate these higher standards?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In this regard, an appellant appears to be required to make two appeals or two petitions − one to appeal against an appealable decision and, two, to request for the appealable decision to not take effect until the Board renders its decision.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Parliamentary Secretary clarify the process and procedure to request an appealable decision not to take effect?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I believe this requires clarification as some subject matter of an appeal could be very time-sensitive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For instance, we introduced the requirement for all arts entertainment to be classified regardless of the venue that they are held at, be it at PE establishments licensed by the Police, such as nightclubs, or at other venues, such as theatres and concert halls.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In line with technological trends, we also made it a requirement for the live streaming of arts entertainment to a public venue to be licensed and classified.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: IMDA agrees that this is important and takes steps to ensure that the public and industry have access to such information.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: First, to inform members of the public interested in staging arts entertainment, IMDA publishes information on the licensing and classification of arts entertainment on its website.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This includes AECC, information on the classification processes, as well as guidelines on the submission of licensing and classification applications.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Second, whenever there are changes to be made to the regulatory framework, IMDA also consults the industry to inform them and seek their views on the proposed changes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For instance, for the 2014 amendment that provides for the classification of arts entertainment regardless of where it is held at, IMDA held several engagement sessions with stakeholders, including SNBA, the Singapore Hotel Association (SHA) and major business precinct associations to inform them of the changes and also to consult them on ways to streamline regulatory processes for PE establishments offering various forms of arts entertainment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For the current round of amendments, IMDA held a briefing to arts groups despite the amendments having little impact on their operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I would also like to address the question from Ms Denise Phua and Mr Murali Pillai on the amendments to section 15A, which would allow IMDA to impose conditions as part of IMDA's classification of arts entertainment that comes under PE licence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The conditions are akin to the existing arts entertainment licensing conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Each arts entertainment should be assessed on its own merit and different conditions may be required depending on the content and the form of the arts entertainment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The more common conditions imposed include the need to display classification ratings and consumer advice at the performance venue, and to prevent persons below the age of 18 from viewing arts entertainment rated R18.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Such conditions are not new, and applicants generally have not had issues complying with them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: First, IMDA adopts an age-based classification framework where content is classified according to their suitability for different age groups.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Classification serves to protect the young, while allowing adults to make informed viewing choices on a wider range of arts content.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In making its classification decisions, IMDA aims to strike a balance between reflecting generally accepted social norms, while giving due consideration to the arts entertainment's artistic and educational merits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Content suitable for a general audience, including children, will be given a General rating, while those that are targeted at a more mature audience can either be rated Advisory, Advisory 16 or R18.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Content that goes beyond the R18 rating, for example, those which may undermine national interest, are likely to cause feelings of ill-will between different racial or religious groups or are excessive and/or exploitative in their depictions, will be disallowed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The existing framework thus already addresses Er Dr Lee Bee Wah's concern about the misuse of arts entertainment as a means to offend or to promote radical ideology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef asked about the breaches that had occurred after the last review of PEMA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: IMDA keeps itself up to date with the developments in the arts scene through engaging stakeholders, such as the Arts Consultative Panel, the National Arts Council and the arts community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: IMDA also reviews the AECC guidelines, as well as its interpretation and application of the guidelines, in consultation with stakeholders to ensure that it keeps up with changes and developments in artistic trends and community standards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But it also means that with higher demand and, therefore, higher supply of arts entertainment, IMDA, as the regulator, will have its work cut out.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: However, through regular engagements and dialogues with the stakeholders, I believe that IMDA will continue to serve its role well in safeguarding the public space for arts entertainment, even as our arts scene continues to become more diverse and vibrant.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Senior Minister of State Janil has addressed the issues raised by Members relating to arts entertainment regulation.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: I will now focus on the issues relating to the regulation of PE.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef and Er Dr Lee Bee Wah asked about the number and seriousness of PE licensing breaches and violent crime in PE establishments.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: About 90% of these breaches were minor, such as failing to maintain a proper record of all employees or failing to ensure that performers do not mingle with patrons.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The situation is under control and Members have also noted this in their speeches.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We are proactively managing the situation, and this Bill strengthens our regulatory levers to ensure that the situation continues to be well-managed.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: As such, we are adopting a calibrated risk-based regulatory regime.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Some Members asked for clarifications on the measures to prevent operation of PE establishments by unsuitable persons or businesses or operated in unsuitable locations.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef and Mr Melvin Yong asked if we can better identify unsuitable persons that hide behind proxies when applying for new licences.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: This is an issue which we take seriously.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: At the point of licence application, the Police will screen the applicant's background carefully to ascertain if he has links to errant establishments, as well as the applicant's general records.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: There are also regular checks that the Police conduct on PE establishments and the operators after the licence application.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Clause 6 of the Bill will also allow the Police to apply certain criteria and requirements on not only the applicant, but also relevant persons, such as responsible officers of the business entity and any person who has substantial interest in or control over the business.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The Police can reject the application, or cancel an issued licence, if any of these relevant persons do not meet the Police's criteria and requirements.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Mr Murali Pillai asked what these criteria and requirements would be.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The criteria include an assessment of honesty, integrity, reputation, competence and capability of the applicant and relevant persons, much like the Liquor Control Act.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: For example, we will consider whether the applicant and relevant persons have been convicted of serious crimes and their track records of complying with regulatory requirements.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The criteria will be published on the Police website when the amendments to the Act take effect.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, Ms Denise Phua and Mr Melvin Yong asked whether there are minimum-distance requirements for the approval of PE establishments near residences, religious places, schools or in mixed-use developments.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Ms Denise Phua also asked for a whole-of-Government approach to determining siting for PE establishments.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Singapore has a highly dense urban environment and it is difficult to impose minimum distances between PE and other land use types.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: A case-by-case approach is taken in such matters.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Specific cases in the Member's constituencies can be taken up separately.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Today, the Police coordinate and work closely with agencies, such as HDB and URA, in assessing applications, and also consider feedback from residents and stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The Police also impose conditions to mitigate potential disamenities to the community, such as acceptable noise limits and limiting operating hours, including limiting the liquor serving hours, if they have a liquor licence.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: This Bill will strengthen the Police's regulatory levers against errant PE establishments.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: I welcome Members to work with their grassroots leaders to engage the Ministry and the relevant Government agencies on how we can use these levers better to manage concerns regarding PE establishments in their constituencies.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Ms Thanaletchimi asked whether the proposal to raise the penalty for providing unlicensed PE is due to the rising incidence of unlicensed PE.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: In 2016, there were only 12 cases of unlicensed PE establishments.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We are proposing to raise the fine for unlicensed PE as a matter of principle.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: A person who disregards the law entirely should be dealt with more harshly than a licensed person who breached licence conditions.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Today, the maximum fine for these offences is the same at $10,000.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Mr Louis Ng asked if a $20,000 fine is a sufficient deterrent for errant operators who try to circumvent our controls and safeguards altogether by operating PE establishments without valid licences.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: If an unlicensed operator is caught but continues to operate illegally while being investigated by the Police, he can be charged for multiple counts of the offence.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: In addition, such operators may also be liable for other offences, for example, the unlicensed sale of liquor under the Liquor Control Act.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The penalties will add up for egregious offenders who brazenly flout the law.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Further, such offenders will not be considered should they seek to apply for PE licences in future, given their history of non-compliance.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef, Mr Louis Ng and Ms Joan Pereira have spoken in support of clause 10, which allows the Licensing Officer to immediately suspend a PE licence, if proceedings have commenced against the licensee or a relevant person of the business for serious crimes.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Mr Murali Pillai asked what type of "proceedings" would trigger suspensions.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: If the licensee or relevant person is not charged, but has other proceedings, such as confiscation orders under the Organised Crime Act outstanding against him, the Police can consider suspending or cancelling the licence under the "fit and proper" framework.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Ms Thanaletchimi asked generally about the basis for suspending or cancelling licences.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar also asked about how the demerit points system works.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: I have addressed these points in my earlier speech.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Dr Lee Bee Wah, Assoc Prof Randolph Tan, Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar, Ms Joan Pereira and Mr Melvin Yong have raised concerns about fights and disamenities in and around PE establishments.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: They have also suggested various measures to deal with these issues.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: This will deter crimes in and around the PE establishment as well as facilitate investigations into any such crimes that take place.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Many responsible PE establishments have already installed such CCTVs.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Some Members have suggested that the Police also hold the licensees responsible for fights and crime that take place outside of their establishments.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Licensees should take reasonable steps to respond to incidents that originate from their premises, even if they spill out of the premises.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: For security officers who are found to be the cause of fights, their licence under the Private Security Industry Act could be revoked.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: For serious criminal offences, they would also be charged in Court.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah also suggested that the Police impose conditions on PE establishments to prohibit their employees from being scantily-clad.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Employees have to be decently attired when carrying out their duties.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: To address the more fundamental issue of establishments that facilitate or attract vice activities, there are licensing conditions to curb such illegal activities.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: I also spoke earlier about the new powers to suspend a licence if the licensee or relevant persons have been charged for serious offences in the Second Schedule.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The Second Schedule includes vice-related offences under the Women's Charter.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: If there is any information on breaches, please call our hotline.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah asked how much resources are committed to regulating PE establishments.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The six Police Land Divisions regularly conduct enforcement checks on PE establishments under their jurisdiction to deter and detect illegal activities.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Clause 5 of the Bill allows the Police to appoint authorised persons to support such checks, in particular, checks of a more routine or preventive nature.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: This provision gives the Police operational flexibility to deploy manpower more effectively or conduct more frequent checks should the need arise.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Authorised persons are also subject to supervisory controls by the Police.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Dr Intan Mokhtar, Mr Louis Ng, Mr Murali Pillai, Ms Denise Phua and Ms Sylvia Lim asked about "suitably trained" authorised persons and their powers.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Examples of "suitably trained" persons include APOs or retired Police Officers who have the requisite skills and experience.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Authorised persons can only exercise the powers of inspection created by clause 17.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: These powers of inspection are tightly scoped to include only the basic powers they need for routine inspections, such as making copies of documents, taking photos or requesting for explanations.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Any licensing breaches detected and reported by authorised persons will be investigated by the Police.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: On Ms Sylvia Lim's and Ms Denise Phua's points, routine inspections, such as checks on staff records, are usually uneventful.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: But in the event of escalation of violence, authorised officers drawn from the ranks of APOs and retired Police Officers would have received training and have experience in managing licensing inspections and managing difficult situations generally, and they can also call for Police back-up.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: APOs today are required to attend basic modules, which include training on checks on persons and bags, and incident management, and they will receive additional training before being deployed to inspect PE establishments.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: On the powers of forced entry for Licensing Officers and Police Officers, Ms Sylvia Lim asked why such powers were needed now.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The Police have encountered PE establishments that locked their premises on arrival of enforcement officers.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: This provides them opportunity to dispose of evidence and lead time to stop any lawful activities.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Currently, a search warrant from the Courts is needed before the Police can gain entry into the premises for the purpose of licensing checks.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The new power of forced entry will allow the Police to take swift and effective action to detect and enforce licensing breaches.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Mr Louis Ng, Ms Denise Phua, Ms Thanaletchimi, Mr Murali Pillai and Ms Sylvia Lim sought clarifications on the structure, processes and terms of reference of the PE Appeal Board.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The Minister for Home Affairs will appoint the members of the PE Appeal Board from a range of fields, such as legal, education and business.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: This ensures that the Appeal Board considers a range of perspectives on issues pertaining to operational matters of PE establishments.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: To maintain independence, the Appeal Board members cannot have any dealings or be in any way concerned with the provision of PE.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Appellants only send written representations to the Board and they can engage lawyers to prepare the representations.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: On whether an appealable decision by the Police will take effect even while the appeal is ongoing, this is not a new provision; it already exists in the current section 16(4) of the Act.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: However, the Appeal Board may decide on a case-by-case basis to specify that the appealable decision should not take effect while the appeal is being considered.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The Appeal Board will strive to hear appeals expeditiously, but time taken depends on various factors, including the complexity of the matter.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The Minister for Home Affairs will prescribe the classes of PE establishment licensees that will have their appeals heard by the Appeal Board.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The Appeal Board would consider the Licensing Officer's considerations regarding the regulation of the PE establishment's operations as well as the appellant's business concerns.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The relevant Ministers will hear appealable decisions from all other licensees that are not prescribed to be heard by the Appeal Board, such as organisers of large-scale, one-off events.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Appeals from such licensees tend to involve security and policy considerations and are more complex, and these are matters of governance where the Minister should decide.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Mr Melvin Yong asked if the Appeal Board will also hear appeals from residents against the approval or renewal of licences for PE establishments.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Our assessment is that there is no need for that.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The Police already take into account residents' and Members' representations on such matters.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: In my earlier speech, I mentioned briefly that following our review, the Police will also work closely with the industry to promote more responsible business operations.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Mr Louis Ng asked whether these industry standards have already been drafted, whether they will be published and eventually will be legislated.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: This is an important effort by the industry to voluntarily adopt higher standards to ensure that PE establishments are operated in a responsible manner.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The laws are adequate, but if the industry wants to do more, they should be encouraged and we welcome it.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan suggested that PE establishments put in effort to promote good drinking etiquette.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah suggested to have additional training for staff to manage disputes.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Ms Thanaletchimi suggested we enhance our public education efforts.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We will work with the industry on these.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Ms Thanaletchimi asked for clarification on the separation of public meetings from PEs as a result of the change to the title of the Act.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: As I have mentioned in my earlier speech, we are removing "Meetings" from the title, as meetings, rallies and forums have been regulated under the Public Order Act since 2009.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair again at 4.10 pm.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 3.45 pm until 4.10 pm.
